主要内容: Starbucks (SBUX) reported a 10% decline in global same-store sales for its fiscal second-quarter in 2020, primarily due to the impact of the coronavirus on its two largest markets, the United States and China. The company also warned that its fiscal third-quarter results would be further affected by the pandemic, even as sales in China began to recover. Starbucks' net income for the quarter was $328.4 million, or 28 cents per share, down from $663.2 million, or 53 cents per share, a year earlier. The company estimated it lost $915 million in sales due to store closures, reduced operating hours, and lower customer traffic. While U.S. same-store sales fell 3%, Chinese sales dropped 50% during the same period. However, Starbucks noted that sales in China have improved as cafes reopened in late February and consumers adapted to the new normal. The company expects same-store sales in China to decline between 15% and 25% in fiscal 2020, with continued rebounds in the second half of the year. About 98% of Chinese cafes have reopened, and Starbucks plans to reopen 90% of its U.S. company-operated locations by early June. Starbucks reported a 10% decline in same-store sales during its Q2 2020 earnings, impacted by the pandemic and social-distancing measures in the U.S. The company noted that negative financial impacts are expected to moderate in the fiscal fourth quarter. Starbucks stated that the impacts of the Covid-19 outbreak are temporary and that its business will fully recover over time. As of March 29, the company had $2.57 billion in cash and cash equivalents. It has suspended its share buyback program but continues to pay investors a quarterly dividend.
